deep.reconstruction:
Context: these 1974 'Topologie modérée' notes set up an axiomatic tame topology. For each n, C_n is a class of subsets of R^n (on the previous page they are assumed compact, condition (*)). C_α-models are sets with a structure locally modelled on members of the C_n. C_α-morphisms are the admissible maps, presumably those whose graphs or coordinate functions lie in the classes. A C_α-space is a locally compact space with a subsheaf of continuous R-valued functions that is locally a C_α-model.

This page adds condition (6): each C_n is stable under finite unions. The empty union shows that the empty set lies in C_n.

Proposition: let X be a model, (X_i) a finite family of C-parts with X = ∪X_i, and f: X → Y a map to a model. Then f is a C-morphism iff every restriction f|X_i is. In modern terms, admissible maps glue along finite closed covers. Proof idea: graph(f) = ∪ graph(f|X_i), which is a finite union, so (6) applies. Continuity is automatic because the pieces are compact, hence closed.

Corollary: in the category of C-models, X is the amalgamated sum (colimit) of the X_i over the pairwise intersections X_i ∩ X_j. So finite closed covers are effective-descent / colimit covers.

Question: does a pushout X ← Z → Y exist in the category of C-models? Grothendieck answers 'OK' under an extension axiom. For every n and X, Y in C_n with Y ⊂ X, every C-morphism f_Y: Y → R extends to a C-morphism f_X: X → R. This is a tame Tietze extension property; Y is closed since it is compact.

The intended argument, standard later, runs as follows. Glue X and Y along a closed embedding Z → X. Using extensions of the coordinate functions, embed X ⊔_Z Y into some R^N, so that the pushout is again a model. This is the step that, for semialgebraic spaces, is Robson's embedding theorem. The marginal '?' suggests he was unsure of the scope, perhaps of the case of non-injective Z → X.

Purpose: show that the tame category is closed under finite gluings and amalgamations. This is the basic requirement for a workable 'tame' topology later advocated in Esquisse d'un programme §5.
errors: The pushout claim ('OK') is justified at best for Z → X a closed embedding (inclusion of a C-part). For an arbitrary morphism Z → X one needs existence of quotients by (definably) proper equivalence relations. The extension axiom alone does not give this; in o-minimal geometry it is a separate nontrivial theorem (van den Dries, ch. 10).

The extension axiom is stated only for R-valued maps. Extension to R^m follows componentwise, but extension into a general model Y (e.g. not a retract of R^m) does not follow. The gluing argument must therefore go through an embedding into R^N, which is not written.
The Proposition implicitly needs the X_i to be closed in X (here guaranteed by compactness via (*)) and a graph-based definition of morphism. Neither is restated on the page.

ideas.what: Axiom: classes C_n of subsets of R^n stable under finite unions (and containing the empty set)
ideas.modern_name: Boolean-closure axioms of an o-minimal structure / semialgebraic or subanalytic class
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86); Shiota's axiomatic classes
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 describes the tame-topology program in general terms only

ideas.what: Morphisms glue along finite covers by C-parts; X is the colimit of the X_i over the X_i ∩ X_j
ideas.modern_name: Gluing lemma for definable maps on finite closed definable covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in semialgebraic/o-minimal geometry (Delfs–Knebusch; van den Dries 'Tame topology')

ideas.what: Existence of pushouts in the tame category deduced from a Tietze-type extension axiom for admissible functions on C-subsets
ideas.modern_name: Definable/semialgebraic Tietze extension theorem and gluing (pushouts) of definable spaces along closed embeddings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic Tietze), Robson 1983 (embedding glued semialgebraic spaces), van den Dries 1998 (definable Tietze, definable quotients)

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1974 isolated, as an axiom of his tame-topology program, a Tietze extension property. He identified it as the key to closure of the tame category under amalgamated sums. This predates the semialgebraic/o-minimal results (Robson 1983; van den Dries 1998) where exactly this mechanism is used. It is a historical priority detail rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: ∀ n ∈ N, X,Y ∈ C_n, Y ⊂ X, et [tout] C_α-morphisme f_Y : Y → R ; ∃ C_α-morphisme f_X : X → R qui le prolonge.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the axiomatic 'what must a tame category satisfy to be closed under gluing' viewpoint (Esquisse §5) had a concrete early form. It is relevant to the history of o-minimality and to categorical treatments of definable spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: Early (1974) and explicit, but the content is the standard gluing lemma plus the now-standard link between Tietze extension and pushouts in semialgebraic/o-minimal geometry. It is mainly of historical-priority interest.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, '$C_n$-modèle' / '$C_n$-morphisme' should likely read '$C_\alpha$-modèle' / '$C_\alpha$-morphisme' (notation of the previous page); '$C_n$-parties' is plausibly '$C_\alpha$-parties'.
'et H [-C_n-]-morphisme' should read 'et tout C_α-morphisme' (the 'H' is likely 'tout' or a ∀-type abbreviation).
'Si on [-petit fonc-] condition suivante' should read 'Si on [a la] condition suivante'.
'2)' at the top is a page/section number, not mathematics.
Marginal note: possibly 'itinéraire donné' or 'intérieur donné' – uncertain; it accompanies a '?' querying the extension condition.
